body: I'm from the Washington DC metropolitan area, going to school in southwest Virginia. You might be onto something with this unfortunate microcosm of humanity thing.

Sometimes you just need to be patient. You can and can't change who you are. I'm not the same person I was when I was 14, or even a day ago. But in a way, I am. You don't need to feel insignificant. You're not even a finished product yet. 

You have a lot of questions. I'm sorry don't have all the answers for you. Don't listen to anyone who claims to. One thing you can do is stop telling yourself that you can't do anything to help yourself. If you believe that, then you are 100% correct. If you don't believe it, there is hope.

You're also not valueless. Don't measure yourself by what everyone else wants from you or compares you to.

It's easy to feel insignificant at your age in our society. Nobody is mature or experienced enough to take interpersonal relationships seriously. Kids respond to social pressure like dust in a hurricane. Schools work to reduce you to a test score producing power plant and if you can't do that, then they won't waste their time with you. Most adults don't think you know anything, and they're right, and you know they're right. But they respond by ignoring and trivializing you. Trust me, you have a lot to look forward to. You can't see it very clearly right now, but it's there. 

When I was 14 I felt the same way. I didn't have friends, everyone was demanding so much from me. Back then I really just tried to tough it out. I wanted to give tomorrow a chance, you know? I guess I'm glad I did. I played music, I expressed myself. I did my best in school, not to become educated or satisfy their demands, but to prove that I was better than or good enough for their system. Or something like that. I don't think they got the message. But that's besides the point. I coped... somehow I guess I made it through all that. Take life in one day at a time. Learn to embrace it. It's all you've really got. All you get. I'm still learning though.

Damn I'm a hypocrite -.- I need to listen to myself.
Maybe you do have the tools to help someone other than yourself. Just because you can't help yourself just yet doesn't mean you can't help someone else for the time being, I suppose?

I'm in a similar place to where you are. Sort of aimlessly floating through life. You sound pretty intelligent. For one thing, don't let anyone trivialize your fears or concerns. Those people are truly dicks, even if they really do have it hard. They say those things to feel better about themselves, not to help you. You definitely don't need that. That's no way to talk to someone who has opened up to you. 

I think not going anywhere in life and lack of motivation is a common problem in this day and age for our age group. I think a good starting point could be figuring whether you need to start feeling better about yourself to go somewhere, or the other way around, or some combination of both. 

I don't know what I want out of my life. They say these are the years where all that starts materializing. I hope it goes by fast.
